slot.brief: Convert aniline to a target substituted arene (figure shows starting amine and product, e.g., to m-bromophenol); choose the correct reagent sequence involving diazotisation and substitution.

stem: For the conversion shown in the figure, choose the correct sequence of reagents.

verdicts.working: Diazotization of aniline followed by CuCN replaces the diazonium group with CN; acidic hydrolysis on heating converts the nitrile to benzoic acid. This is option A.

working:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2\xrightarrow[273\text{–}278\,\text{K}]{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}}\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-\xrightarrow{\text{CuCN}}\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN}\xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+,\ heat}\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$.

Independent check: Diazotization of aniline followed by CuCN replaces the diazonium group with CN; acidic hydrolysis on heating converts the nitrile to benzoic acid. This is option A.
solution:
Aniline undergoes diazotization, then the diazonium group is replaced by $\text{CN}$ using $\text{CuCN}$; acidic hydrolysis of the nitrile gives benzoic acid.
$$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2\xrightarrow[273\text{–}278\,\text{K}]{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}}\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-\xrightarrow{\text{CuCN}}\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN}\xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+,\ heat}\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$$

figure.description: Draw aniline on the left as a benzene ring with an –NH2 group at one vertex, and benzoic acid on the right as a benzene ring with a –C(=O)OH group at one vertex. Connect them with a horizontal reaction arrow pointing left to right. Do not label reagents or conditions.

draft.distractor_notes: B: CuCl gives chlorobenzene instead of the nitrile. C: Hydrogenation reduces the nitrile rather than hydrolysing it. D: KI gives iodobenzene.
